title: Twenty-six hours in Boston
subtitle: A loose Saturday 1 p.m. to Sunday 3 p.m. sequence by train, with room to linger.
premise: Back Bay on foot Saturday afternoon, Cambridge and Allston by subway and bus Saturday evening, then the night at Maverick Suites on Newbury Street. Sunday is based at The Arcadian Hotel in Brookline.
flexibility: Clock times are a suggested order. Sort the list by time, or by walking distance from Maverick Suites on Saturday and The Arcadian Hotel on Sunday.

days.label: Saturday
days.summary: Bookstore lunch, Newbury Street, matcha, the Common, then Harvard Square and HEYTEA.

days.label: Sunday
days.summary: Based at The Arcadian Hotel in Brookline. Harvard Pond is no longer on this trip.

items.title: Trident Booksellers & Cafe
items.summary: Lunch and a long browse in the indie bookstore-cafe at the Mass Ave end of Newbury.
items.description: Trident has been a Back Bay bookstore and full-service cafe since 1984. The room is half restaurant, half shelves: all-day breakfast, lunch, and dinner, plus magazines, cards, and a deep book floor. Saturday midday is one of the busiest times, so treat 1 p.m. as a landing and let the table run long. If the room is loud, the visit still works as a shorter meal plus a lap of the shelves.
highlights: Two floors of books inside a working cafe
All-day breakfast through dinner
Quieter if you slide toward mid-afternoon rather than noon brunch
items.hours: Daily 8:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas.
items.visit: A meal and a browse usually lands around 90 minutes. Bookish lingering can stretch past two hours.
nearby: Newbury Street begins outside the door
Hynes Convention Center station, Green Line, is the closest T stop
Commonwealth Avenue Mall is one block north

sources.label: Trident hours and location
OpenTable: daily 8 a.m.–10 p.m. and weekend rush notes

items.title: Step onto Newbury and walk east
items.summary: No train. Trident sits between Hereford Street and Massachusetts Avenue, so the rest of the street is a walk toward the Public Garden.
items.description: Head east, toward Arlington Street. Cross streets run alphabetically from Hereford down to Arlington, so it is hard to get lost. The shops get dressier as the address numbers drop.

transit.to: Newbury Street, heading toward Arlington Street
transit.minutes: About 10 minutes before you want to start ducking into shops
transit.note: Stay on Newbury. Boylston Street is one block south if you want a quieter parallel.

sources.label: Trident: closest T is Hynes; block between Hereford and Mass Ave

items.title: Newbury Street
items.address: Newbury Street, Arlington Street to Massachusetts Avenue
items.summary: A mile of brownstone shops, galleries, and sidewalk tables, walked from the casual west end toward the Public Garden.
items.description: The famous stretch is about eight blocks and a mile, from Massachusetts Avenue to Arlington Street at the Public Garden. The west end is the more independent, bohemian side. Closer to Arlington the storefronts turn toward galleries and higher-end fashion. Walking it without stops takes 15–20 minutes. With windows, side streets, and one deliberate shop, give it an hour and a half. Commonwealth Avenue Mall and the Boston Public Library at Copley Square are easy detours if the street feels crowded.
highlights: Victorian brownstones converted into shops and cafes
Character shifts from eclectic at Mass Ave to polished at Arlington
Open Newbury Street days sometimes close the road to cars; check the city calendar
items.hours: The street itself is always open. Individual shops set their own hours, and many close by early evening.
items.visit: 1.5–3 hours if you shop. This plan uses about 90 minutes so the park still gets daylight.
nearby: Boston Public Library and Copley Square, one block south
Commonwealth Avenue Mall, one block north
Green Line: Hynes (west end), Copley (middle), Arlington (Public Garden end)

sources.label: Newbury Street, east end at Arlington, west toward Mass Ave

items.title: Walk to Blank Street
items.summary: One block south of Newbury, at Boylston and Dartmouth.
items.description: From the Dartmouth Street crossing on Newbury, walk one block south to Boylston Street. Blank Street is on that corner. There is no Newbury Street Blank Street on the current store list; this Back Bay shop is the one that sits on the walk you are already doing.

transit.note: Copley station (Green Line) is also at this corner if you arrived by train instead.

sources.label: Blank Street, Boylston & Dartmouth

items.title: Blank Street Coffee
items.summary: A matcha stop at Boylston and Dartmouth, between Newbury and the Public Garden.
items.description: This is the Back Bay Blank Street, a block off the east end of Newbury. Order a matcha — the menu rotates seasonal versions alongside the regular latte — and drink it while you cross into the garden. Seating is limited, so plan on a short stop or a to-go cup. A second Blank Street sits in Harvard Square at 1380 Massachusetts Avenue if you would rather have the matcha there on Saturday evening; that shop is open until 9 p.m. on Saturday.
highlights: Matcha and coffee, built for a short ritual
Sits between the shopping street and the parks
Harvard Square shop is the alternate if you want the drink later
items.hours: Monday–Saturday 6:30 a.m.–9:00 p.m. Sunday 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.
items.visit: 20–40 minutes. The line moves quickly; the linger is optional.
nearby: Public Garden entrance across Arlington Street
Copley Square and the Boston Public Library

sources.label: Boylston & Dartmouth hours and address
Harvard Square alternate: 1380 Massachusetts Avenue

items.title: Walk into the Public Garden
items.summary: Cross Arlington Street. The garden is the landscaped half; the Common is just beyond Charles Street.
items.description: From Boylston and Dartmouth, walk east to Arlington Street and enter the Public Garden. Cross the lagoon bridge, then Charles Street, and you are on Boston Common. Arlington station is directly across from the garden if you would rather ride the Green Line one stop from Copley.

transit.to: Boston Public Garden and Boston Common
transit.line: On foot, or Green Line Copley to Arlington
transit.note: Park Street and Boylston stations sit on the Common itself if you continue east.

items.title: Boston Common and the Public Garden
items.address: Boston Common, between Tremont, Park, Beacon, and Charles Streets
items.summary: The garden lagoon, then the Common’s lawns, Frog Pond, and the start of the Freedom Trail.
items.description: Do the Public Garden first, while the light is still on the lagoon and the George Washington statue. The Swan Boats run on that lagoon from mid-April through Labor Day; the 2026 season ended September 7, so later in September the ride is a view, not a ticket. Cross Charles Street onto Boston Common, the older and more open park. The visitor center is at 139 Tremont Street, the Freedom Trail’s red line starts between Park Street and Boylston, and the Frog Pond is the seasonal skating and splash landmark. Beacon Hill’s brick streets begin on the north side of the Common if you still have legs.
highlights: Public Garden lagoon and bridge
Freedom Trail start and the visitor center on Tremont
Frog Pond, Parkman Bandstand, and a Beacon Hill edge if you want one more walk
items.hours: Parks open 6:30 a.m.–11:00 p.m., free, every day. Pedestrian access is 24 hours.
items.visit: 45–90 minutes for the highlights. Two hours if you add Beacon Hill.
nearby: Beacon Hill and Charles Street shops and restaurants
Park Street station (Red and Green Lines) and Boylston (Green Line)
Arlington station for the garden side

items.title: Red Line to Harvard Square
items.summary: Park Street to Harvard, no transfer.
items.description: Walk to Park Street station at Park and Tremont, on the Common. Take the Red Line outbound toward Alewife and get off at Harvard. The ride itself is about 12 minutes. Saturday evening trains are frequent; still check the app if there is a disruption.

transit.minutes: About 12 minutes on the train, plus walking into the station
transit.note: You exit into the square. Follow signs for Harvard Yard or Brattle Street depending on which side you want first.

sources.label: Harvard to Park Street is about 12 minutes
Harvard Square via the Red Line

items.title: Harvard Square
items.summary: Dinner and a night loop of the square, the Yard gates, and the walk toward the river.
items.description: Harvard Square is the triangle where Massachusetts Avenue, Brattle Street, and JFK Street meet, and it is open around the clock even when the shops are not. Saturday evening still has restaurants, buskers, and people moving through the plaza. Harvard Yard’s gates are beside the station; Massachusetts Hall and the main lawn are worth a slow circuit. If you want daylight browsing — Harvard Book Store, the museums, a longer river walk — move this block to Sunday morning and keep the pond visit short enough to catch the 12:25 p.m. train back. The Harvard Square Blank Street at 1380 Massachusetts Avenue is open until 9 p.m. Saturday if you skipped matcha in Back Bay.
highlights: Out of the station and into the plaza
Harvard Yard at night, just east of the square
Dinner on Brattle, JFK, or Mt. Auburn, then a walk toward the Charles if you have time
items.hours: The square is always open. Shops and museums keep their own hours and many close by early evening. Restaurants run later.
items.visit: Two hours is a solid daytime visit. This evening block is about 90 minutes, with dinner included. A half-day if you add the museums.
nearby: Harvard Book Store on Massachusetts Avenue
Blank Street at 1380 Massachusetts Avenue, until 9 p.m. Saturday
Charles River and JFK Park, a short walk south

sources.label: City of Cambridge: Harvard Square
Harvard Square Business Association: Red Line
About two hours, or half a day with the Yard and museums

items.title: Bus 66 to HEYTEA
items.summary: From Harvard Square toward Allston. Get off where the bus meets the Green Line B at Harvard Avenue.
items.description: Route 66 runs between Harvard Square and Nubian and passes Harvard Avenue at Commonwealth Avenue, the Allston stop for HEYTEA. Board toward Nubian, not toward Harvard. The ride is often about 20–30 minutes; Saturday night traffic on North Harvard Street can add time. If the bus is slow, the fallback is the Red Line back to Park Street and the Green Line B out to Harvard Ave, which is longer.

transit.fare: Bus fare, often covered by a recent contactless subway tap. Confirm in the MBTA app.
transit.note: HEYTEA is a short walk from that stop, at 162 Harvard Avenue. The Green Line B Harvard Ave station is on the same corner for the ride home.

sources.label: Route 66 connects Harvard Square to Harvard Ave at Commonwealth

items.title: HEYTEA Allston
items.summary: A to-go fruit tea or matcha on Harvard Avenue, before the shop closes at 10.
items.description: Boston’s HEYTEA is on Harvard Avenue in Allston, not in Harvard Square. Drinks are made to order — fruit tea, milk tea, and matcha, often with a cheese or cloud foam — so a line can take a while even late. The shop is small and is generally a takeaway stop, with little or no seating. Arrive before 9:45 if you want a cushion before the 10 p.m. close. Drink it on the walk to the Green Line.
highlights: Fresh fruit teas and matcha, customizable sugar and ice
Green Line B is on the corner for the trip back
Allston Village storefronts along Harvard Avenue if anything is still open
items.visit: 20–40 minutes, mostly the line and the walk away with the cup.
nearby: Green Line B, Harvard Avenue station
Bus 66 back toward Harvard Square or on toward Brookline
Allston’s Harvard Avenue restaurants, earlier in the evening

sources.label: HEYTEA Allston opening, 162 Harvard Avenue
Hours: daily 11:30 a.m.–10 p.m., takeaway-style shop

items.summary: Harvard Ave inbound to Copley, then a one-block walk to 245 Newbury Street.
items.description: Board the Green Line B inbound toward Government Center and get off at Copley. Maverick Suites is one block north, at 245 Newbury Street.

transit.to: Copley, then walk to 245 Newbury Street
transit.minutes: About 20–30 minutes to the Back Bay stops
transit.note: Copley is the closest stop to Maverick Suites. Hynes is the stop if you are coming from the Mass Ave end of Newbury earlier in the day.

items.title: Night at Maverick Suites
items.summary: Saturday night at Maverick Suites, on Newbury between Exeter and Fairfield.
items.description: End the night at Maverick Suites, 245 Newbury Street. From HEYTEA, take the Green Line B inbound and get off at Copley, then walk one block north to Newbury. This is the point Saturday distances are measured from.
highlights: 245 Newbury Street, a short walk from Copley
Saturday distances in the list use this address
